title: Finalize risk badge visual system + tooltip copy (Optimization Suggestions beta)
creator: Tessa Morgan
content:
Goal
Finalize the risk badge visual system and tooltip/explanatory copy used in the Suggestions list + details drawer. This must be: (a) accessible (color contrast + non-color cues), (b) unambiguous that “risk” refers to performance/reliability/quality risk (not security), and (c) consistent with Risk model v0 thresholds.

Scope
- Badges: Low / Medium / High (and “Unknown” handling if confidence too low)
- Tooltip copy on hover/focus in the table column header and per-row badge
- Inline microcopy in details drawer: what the risk means + recommended guardrails
- Accessibility checks: contrast ratios, focus states, tooltip keyboard support, screen reader labels

Non-goals
- Redefining risk thresholds (owned by Applied ML + ENG; see ADR)
- Introducing new risk labels (e.g., “Severe”, numeric scores) for beta

Background / context
We’ve seen early feedback that stakeholders interpret “risk” as security/compliance. We need consistent language to clarify this is operational risk: impact to p95 latency, timeout rate, and user-visible quality changes.

References
- Confluence: risk definitions + copy guidelines: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/risk-level-definition-and-copy-guidelines.json
- ADR: v0 risk scoring model: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-risk-scoring-model-v0.json
- Slack design thread (contrast + wording): sources/slack/design/1771703310-risk-badge-copy-and-color-contrast.json
- Design flow context: DES-627 (details drawer explanations), DES-611 (table layout/filters)

Proposed visual system (beta)
Badges
- Low: “Low risk”
- Medium: “Medium risk”
- High: “High risk”
- Unknown: “Risk unknown” (only when confidence band too wide or insufficient telemetry)

Iconography (non-color cue)
- Low: check icon
- Medium: triangle/warning icon
- High: alert/octagon icon
- Unknown: question mark icon

Color usage
- Use color as secondary signal only; badges must be readable and distinguishable in grayscale.
- Low: neutral/green-tinted background
- Medium: amber/yellow-tinted background
- High: red-tinted background
- Unknown: gray background

Accessibility notes
- Badge text must meet WCAG contrast requirements against badge background.
- Do not rely on hue alone: include icon + text label.
- Tooltip must be reachable by keyboard (tab to badge) and readable by screen readers (aria-describedby).

Tooltip copy (final draft for review)
Column header tooltip (table)
Title: “Risk level”
Body: “Risk estimates the likelihood that applying this suggestion impacts performance or reliability (e.g., p95 latency or timeouts). It is not a security risk rating.”
Footer link (optional): “How risk is calculated” → deep link to docs section.

Per-row badge tooltip
- Low risk: “Low likelihood of negative performance impact. Safe to try with a standard canary and rollback plan.”
- Medium risk: “Some likelihood of performance impact under peak load. Use a canary, monitor p95 latency/timeouts, and ramp gradually.”
- High risk: “Higher likelihood of performance impact for this route/model. Apply only with tight guardrails (small canary, slower ramp, and clear rollback criteria).”
- Risk unknown: “Not enough telemetry to estimate risk confidently. Add more traffic/telemetry or revisit later.”

Details drawer microcopy (summary line)
- Low: “This change is unlikely to affect p95 latency for typical traffic patterns.”
- Medium: “This change may increase p95 latency during peak concurrency; monitor closely during rollout.”
- High: “This change is likely to increase p95 latency or timeout rate without careful rollout controls.”
- Unknown: “We can’t estimate performance impact reliably with current telemetry.”

Guardrails (copy used in details drawer)
- Always include: “Roll out gradually with a canary and be ready to roll back.”
- For Medium/High: explicitly call out what to watch in Console dashboards: p95 latency, error rate/timeouts, queue depth (if exposed), and saturation signals.

Open questions
1) Should we say “performance risk” instead of “risk” everywhere?
- Proposal: Keep column header “Risk level” for brevity, but tooltip + drawer always say “performance/reliability risk.”

2) Should “Unknown” show as badge in list or only as empty/‘—’?
- Proposal: Show “Risk unknown” badge so users understand it’s a limitation, not a bug.

3) Do we need an explicit “Quality risk” mention?
- Proposal: Mention “quality changes” only in details drawer when suggestion might change output distribution (rare for batching/caching; mostly latency/reliability). For beta, keep list tooltips focused on performance/reliability to reduce confusion.

Acceptance criteria
- Badge component spec finalized and shared with ENG (states, icons, colors, spacing).
- Tooltip copy approved by PM (Marissa/Aditya) and Docs (Elliot) for consistency with public-facing phrasing.
- Accessibility checks complete:
  - Contrast ratios documented for each badge state
  - Keyboard focus + tooltip behavior validated
  - Screen reader label strings finalized
- Hand-off notes posted in Linear and linked in ENG-19358.

Progress updates
- 2026-02-03 (Kenji): Drafted tooltip copy variants; reduced ambiguity by explicitly stating “not a security risk rating.” Shared in design Slack thread for feedback.
- 2026-02-07 (Alicia): Ran initial contrast checks on badge backgrounds vs text at 12–13px. Medium (amber) failed contrast on light theme with white text; switching to dark text resolves.
- 2026-02-10 (Tessa): Alignment with PM: keep “Risk level” label; ensure tooltip contains the “not security” line. Request to keep tooltip ≤ 2 sentences + optional docs link.
- 2026-02-14 (George): Usability study note (3 sessions): “risk” misread as security until participants saw tooltip. Recommendation: make the tooltip discoverable via (i) info icon in header and (ii) focus-visible outline on badge.
- 2026-02-18 (Kenji): Updated spec to include icons + text in badge (no color-only). Added “Risk unknown” state.
- 2026-02-22 (Kenji): Hand-off draft posted to ENG-19358 comment with copy strings and a11y requirements; waiting on final approval from Docs for wording.

Requested reviewers
- Tessa Morgan (Design lead)
- Marissa Cole (PM, Console)
- Aditya Rao (PM, Optimize)
- Elliot Price (Docs)
- Leila Farouk (QA/a11y spot check)

Next steps
- Finalize wording with Docs (ensure consistent “estimated” phrasing).
- Confirm with ENG if we can add an info icon next to the Risk column header in the table (if not, ensure header tooltip triggers on hover/focus reliably).
- After approval, mark Done and link to the implementing PR once merged (risk badge component + tooltips).
